what_its_for: Futibatinib is a cancer medicine used to treat a type of bile duct cancer (called cholangiocarcinoma) that has spread or cannot be removed by surgery. It works specifically in patients whose cancer has a certain gene change (called an FGFR2 fusion or rearrangement), which your doctor will confirm with a special test before starting this medicine.
how_to_take: Take futibatinib by mouth (as a tablet) once a day. You can take it with or without food. Swallow the tablet whole — do not crush, chew, or split it. Try to take it at the same time every day to help you remember. If you vomit after taking your dose, do NOT take an extra dose — just take your next scheduled dose as usual.
dosing: The usual dose is 20 mg (one tablet) taken once daily. Your doctor may lower your dose or temporarily stop your medicine if you experience certain side effects. Always take exactly the dose your doctor prescribes — do not change your dose on your own.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose and your next scheduled dose is more than 12 hours away, take the missed dose as soon as you remember. If your next dose is less than 12 hours away, skip the missed dose and just take your next dose at the regular time. Never take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store futibatinib tablets at room temperature between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep them in the original container with the lid tightly closed. Keep this medicine away from moisture and heat. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Ask your pharmacist how to safely dispose of any unused tablets.
what_to_avoid: Avoid grapefruit and grapefruit juice while taking this medicine, as it can increase the amount of drug in your blood and raise your risk of side effects. Tell your doctor and pharmacist about ALL other medicines, vitamins, and herbal supplements you take, because many drugs can interact with futibatinib. Avoid strong antacids or medications that significantly reduce stomach acid without first asking your doctor. Women should avoid becoming pregnant during treatment and for at least 1 week after the last dose. Men with female partners who could become pregnant should use effective birth control during treatment and for 1 week after the last dose. Do not breastfeed during treatment and for 1 week after the last dose.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor right away if you experience any of the following: changes in your vision or eye problems (blurry vision, dry eyes, seeing flashing lights, or sensitivity to light); mouth sores or pain that make it hard to eat or drink; unusual nail changes (nail pain, separation, or infection); skin redness, dryness, peeling, or rash on your hands and feet; high phosphate levels in your blood (your doctor will monitor this with blood tests); signs of liver problems such as yellowing of your skin or eyes, dark urine, or severe stomach pain; kidney problems such as decreased urination or swelling in your legs; or any severe or unusual symptoms that concern you.
when_it_works: Everyone responds differently to cancer treatment. Your doctor will check how well the medicine is working through regular imaging scans (such as CT scans) and blood tests. Some patients notice improvements within the first few months of treatment. Keep taking your medicine as directed even if you do not feel differently, and talk to your doctor if you have concerns about how the treatment is going.
special_populations: Pregnancy and breastfeeding: This medicine can harm an unborn baby. Do not use if you are pregnant. Do not breastfeed while taking this medicine. Liver problems: Your doctor may adjust your dose if you have moderate to severe liver disease. Kidney problems: No dose adjustment is typically needed for mild to moderate kidney disease, but your doctor will monitor you closely. Older adults: Older patients may be more sensitive to side effects, so let your doctor know right away if you notice any new or worsening symptoms. Children: This medicine has not been studied in patients under 18 years of age and is not currently approved for use in children.
